Subject: Geo operations checklist: legal vs technical constraints & proposed next steps

Hi Anna,

Thanks again for the time today — good conversation and helpful context on the regulatory constraints you’re balancing across DE/FR clinics. Per our call, I captured the specific items we agreed to follow up on so your legal and infra teams can validate feasibility. Please see below; I’ve attached a compact checklist (redwood-residency-checklist-v1.pdf) and your spreadsheet back for reference.

Summary (short):
- Objective: Keep PHI-derived inference data for EU patients strictly within EU regions; allow aggregated non-PII telemetry to cross regions for analytics.
- Primary asks from MedicaSys: EU-only residency for request/response payloads tied to patient records, cross-region failover capability for DR that never persists primary patient data outside EU, and 7-year archival retention policy with audit logs.

Questions / Action items we promised to validate:
1) Data flow separation: Can Redwood guarantee that request payloads tagged as "EU-PHI" will only be routed to EU-backed hosts and that any fallback to non-EU regions will be a warm-standby read-only mode with no primary persistence outside EU?
2) Backup snapshot residency: What are typical backup/restore behaviors for Dedicated vs Private deployments? Can snapshots be pinned to EU object stores?
3) Audit logs and KMS: Do audit logs contain payloads? If not, how long are token-level logs retained and what controls exist for rotation/export to your SIEM? Can we integrate with a customer-managed KMS?
4) Retention/Deletion: Confirm ability to enforce per-customer retention policies (7y) and provide certified deletion receipts for specific patient-related datasets.

Next steps (proposed):
- Monica will send a short tech note with exact config knobs (pinning, backup policy selectors, KMS options) by tomorrow EOD.
- Redwood will draft a proposed language for the residency clause to be reviewed by Olivia in legal.
- We will schedule a short 30-min session with your infra and legal next week to align on failover semantics.

Attachments: redwood-residency-checklist-v1.pdf (checklist), medicasys-data-classification.csv (your classification export you shared during the demo).

Thanks — I’ll loop in more detail in the follow-up from Monica.

Best,

Karthik / Monica,

Appreciate the clear summary. A few clarifications from security before we lock proposal language: 

1) Failover semantics: Warm-standby is acceptable only if no patient-identifiable request or response is ever written to disks in a non-EU region. Can you confirm that failover instances will run in a memory-only mode until the operator triggers a controlled restore to EU? We need the guarantee to be provable for auditors.

2) Snapshots: Our procurement prefers snapshots stored in an EU S3 bucket under our account. Will Redwood support customer-owned object store for backups in Private or Dedicated plans? If not, what encryption + tenancy separation is used?

3) Logs: We must ensure audit logs do NOT contain PII. Token-level traces are fine but must have redaction. How long do you keep request metadata vs full request/response bodies?

4) Key management: We prefer to bring our own KMS/HSM for key control and key-rotation events. Is there a supported integration and what role does Redwood maintain vs customer?

Also looping Olivia (legal) for retention and deletion receipts.

-James

Hi James / Anna — thanks for the questions. Below is a concise technical response to each item; happy to expand in the call if helpful. I also attached a one-page config map (redwood-residency-checklist-v1.pdf) with the exact flags to set per deployment type.

1) Failover semantics: For Dedicated and Private deployments we support region-affinity routing with a strict "pin" attribute on request metadata. If a request is tagged EU-PHI, the router will only send traffic to EU hosts. For cross-region failover we provide two options:
   - Passive failover (recommended): Non-EU warm standby receives only health checks and control-plane sync; it does NOT accept live traffic until an operator issues an explicit, auditable failover command. No disk-based persistence of EU-PHI occurs in the standby.
   - Active failover (for non-PHI workloads): Automatic cross-region route with persisted replicas.

We log failover actions (operator ID, timestamp, reason) and these entries are separate from request payload logs.

2) Snapshots and backups: Private deployments can be configured to use customer-owned S3-compatible storage (EU region) for periodic snapshots. For Dedicated we offer either Redwood-managed object stores (encrypted, tenant-separated keys) or customer-provided buckets for backups depending on the contract. Snapshots that contain PHI can be restricted to EU buckets only.

3) Logs and redaction: By default Redwood retains token/latency/route-level metadata for 90 days. Request/response bodies are not included in audit logs unless explicitly enabled; when enabled, redaction rules can be applied. We provide out-of-the-box redaction for known PHI patterns and integrate with customer SIEM export via secure syslog or S3 export. We can also run an ingestion-level filter for additional patterns you supply.

4) KMS/HSM: We support customer-managed KMS integrations (AWS KMS BYOK, external HSM via PKCS#11) for Private and Dedicated. Redwood can be configured to have zero-access to plaintext keys for certain key policies. Key-rotation events and audit logs are available via the console and can be exported to your SIEM.

Proposed next steps:
- I’ll build a short runbook showing the exact config to enforce EU-only residency and the CLI/console steps to trigger a controlled failover. Expect that by EOD today.
- Karthik / Grace: can you propose 2x 30-min slots next week for legal + infra?

Attachments: redwood-residency-checklist-v1.pdf (config map).

Thanks,
